$comment: Who sits on the review panel. Seats are counted by FAMILY, not by id — see
panel.ts. Two seats sharing a family are one vote, because they share their
blind spots.
COST. Every seat with "enabled": true is an OpenRouter `:free` variant. That
is not a cheap tier, it is a structural zero: a `:free` model cannot bill the
platform key at all, which is the invariant lib/ai/openrouter.ts enforces and
the reason the existing Stop-hook verifier can run on the shared key. Adding
a paid seat is a spend decision (rule 31), so paid seats ship disabled.
The free-model landscape shifts weekly. Re-check these ids against
openrouter.ai/collections/free-models when a seat starts failing; a model
that has been withdrawn shows up as a failed seat, which the panel reports
rather than silently counting as agreement.

seats.note: The default the repo already runs for Margot and the Stop verifier. Quality 60, 1M context, built for agentic work.
A genuinely different family, and the highest generic-quality free model at the last review (Quality 65, 262K). This seat is what makes the panel a panel.

SAME FAMILY as nemotron-super, deliberately. It adds depth, not independence: when both Nemotron seats agree and Gemma does not, that is one vote against one, not two against one. panel.ts enforces this by counting families.

A third independent family, and the strongest available. Off by default because it bills per token: a ChatGPT Plus/Pro plan does NOT authenticate this — plan subscriptions cover the ChatGPT apps and Codex CLI signed in on your own machine, while an API call from a CI runner needs a separately-billed platform key. Enable only with the owner's spend decision.

A third genuinely independent family, and the panel's paid seat. The owner authorised it in session on 2026-09-02. Model id, base URL and prices verified against MiniMax's own OpenAPI spec at platform.minimax.io on the same day, not assumed: the enum is MiniMax-M3 / M2.7 / M2.5 / M2.1 / M2 (with -highspeed variants), and M2.5 is the value pick at $0.30 per M input and $1.20 per M output. A 120KB diff plus REVIEW.md is roughly 40K input and 2K output, so about 1.5 US cents per pull request. Two things to keep straight: this is api.minimax.io, NOT the third-party minimax-m2.com deployment that also advertises an OpenAI-compatible endpoint at different prices; and it is /v1/chat/completions, NOT the /v2/video_generation endpoint the same account uses for MiniMax-H3. Consider M3 if diffs start exceeding M2.5's 204,800-token context — it carries 1M and is the coding SOTA, at a price to confirm.

$comment: Called ONLY when the free panel splits on a Critical finding — one family
says a security or data-loss defect exists and the others do not. That is
the one question worth paying to settle, because both possible errors are
expensive: shipping the defect, or crying wolf until reviews get ignored.
It is not a reviewer. It sees the contested finding and the diff, and
answers whether the finding stands. Everything else stays free.
Disabled until the owner makes the spend decision. While disabled, a
contested Critical is reported as an unconfirmed lead and says so.
